options:
Ratio of work functions $\phi_1: \phi_2: \phi_3=1: 2: 4$.

Ratio of work functions $\phi_1: \phi_2: \phi_3=4: 2: 1$.

$\tan \theta$ is directly proportional to $h c / e$, where $h$ is Planck's constant and $c$ is the speed of light.

The violet colour light can eject photoelectrons from metals 2 and 3.
questions.solution:
From the relation, $e V=\frac{h c}{\lambda}-\phi$ or $V=\left(\frac{h c}{e}\right)\left(\frac{1}{\lambda}\right)-\frac{\phi}{e}$ This is equation of straight line.
Slope is $\tan \theta=\frac{h c}{e}$
\begin{aligned}
\phi_1: \phi_2: \phi_3 & =\frac{h c}{\lambda_{01}}: \frac{h c}{\lambda_{02}}: \frac{h c}{\lambda_{03}}=\frac{1}{\lambda_{01}}: \frac{1}{\lambda_{02}}: \frac{1}{\lambda_{03}}=1: 2: 4 \\
\frac{1}{\lambda_{01}} & =0.001 \mathrm{~nm}^{-1} \text { or } \lambda_{01}=10000 Å \\
\frac{1}{\lambda_{02}} & =0.002 \mathrm{~nm}^{-1} \text { or } \lambda_{02}=5000 Å \\
\frac{1}{\lambda_{03}} & =0.004 \mathrm{~nm}^{-1} \text { or } \lambda_{03}=25000 Å
\end{aligned}

Violet colour has wavelength $4000 Å$.
So, violet colour can eject photoelectrons from metal-1 and metal-2.

questions.q: Graph shows the variation of de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ versus $\frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$ where $V$ is the accelerating potential for four particles, P, Q, R, S carrying same charge but of mass $m_1, m_2, m_3, m_4$. Which one represents a particle of smaller mass?
questions.solution:
De-broglie wavelength,
$\lambda=\frac{h}{p}$
Kinetic energy :
$\begin{aligned}
& K=\frac{p^2}{2 m}=q V \\
& \lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m q V}}
\end{aligned}$
Slope of straight line
$\tan \theta=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m q}}$
Hence, more is slope of line, less is the mass.

questions.q: Graph shows the variation of de-Broglie wavelength $(\lambda)$ versus $\frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$ where ' $V$ ' is the accelerating potential for four particles A, B, C, $\mathrm{D}$ carrying same charge but of masses $\mathrm{m}_1, \mathrm{~m}_2$, $\mathrm{m}_3, \mathrm{~m}_4$. Which on represents a particle of largest mass?
questions.solution:
de Broglie wayelength $\lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{p}}\therefore \quad \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mqv}}}\therefore \quad \lambda \sqrt{\mathrm{v}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mq}}} \Rightarrow \frac{\lambda}{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{v}}}\right)}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mq}}}\therefore \quad$ Slope of the graph $=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mq}}}$
The slope will be maximum for minimum mass.
$\therefore \quad \mathrm{m}_4$ is minimum and $\mathrm{m}_1$ will be minimum.

questions.q:
Assertion (A) Electromagnetic waves exert pressure, called radiation pressure.
Reason (R) This is because they carry energy.
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are true and $R$ is a correct explanation for $\mathrm{A}$.
Both $A$ and $R$ are true but $R$ is not a correct explanation for $\mathrm{A}$.
questions.solution:
Electromagnetic waves (EMW) exerts pressure, called radiation pressure.
In perfect reflecting waves, $p=2 I / C$
In perfect absorbing waves, $p=I / C$
So, Assertion is true.
EMW exert pressure on the surface because they carry energy also.
Therefore reason is also true.
But, Reason (R) is not a correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.q:
Assertion (A) The colour of radiation does not change on passing through different media.
Reason (R) The media do not absorb or emit colours.
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are true and $R$ is a correct explanation for $A$.
Both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true but $\mathrm{R}$ is not a correct explanation for $\mathrm{A}$.
A is false but $R$ is true.
questions.solution:
The colour of radiation does not change on passing through different media. This is because, when light radiation passes through different media, only wavelength and speed changes, but frequency remains same and colour of light radiation depends only on frequency.
Hence, Assertion (A) is true.
"The media do not absorb or emit colours" this statement is wrong. Because the absorption or emission of colours of radiation depends only on the nature of medium.
Hence, Reason is false.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : The photoelectric effect does not take place, if the energy of the incident radiation is less than the work function of a metal.

Reason R : Kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is zero, if the energy of the incident radiation is equal to the work function of a metal.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
questions.solution:
Work function of a metal is defined as the minimum amount of energy needed for ejection of photoelectron. Therefore, Assertion is correct.

Incident energy may or may not be completely absorbed by the photoelectron. Therefore, kinetic energy of a photoelectron may be zero even if the incident radiation has energy greater than work function. Hence, though the reason is correct, it is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $\mathbf{A}$ and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Number of photons increases with increase in frequency of light.
Reason R: Maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons increases with the frequency of incident radiation.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are correct and $\mathbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$.
Both $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{R}$ are correct and $\mathbf{R}$ is NOT the correct explanation of $\mathbf{A}$.
$\mathbf{A}$ is not correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is correct.
$\mathbf{A}$ is correct but $\mathbf{R}$ is not correct.
questions.solution:
Intensity of light $\mathrm{I}=\frac{\mathrm{nh} \nu}{\mathrm{A}}$ Here $\mathrm{n}$ is no. of photons per unit time. $\mathrm{n}=\frac{\mathrm{IA}}{\mathrm{h} \nu}$ so on increasing frequency $v, \mathrm{n}$ decreases taking intensity constant. $\mathrm{k}_{\max }=\mathrm{h} v-\phi$
So on increasing $v$, kinetic energy increases.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements $A$ and $B$ and identify the correct choice in the given answers.
A. Tightly bound electrons of target material scatter $X$-ray photon, resulting in the Compton effect.
B. Photoelectric effect takes place with free electrons.
questions.solution:
Statement A: "Tightly bound electrons of target material scatter X-ray photon, resulting in the Compton effect."
This is false. The Compton effect involves the scattering of X-ray photons by free or loosely bound electrons. Tightly bound electrons are more likely to participate in the photoelectric effect, not Compton scattering.
Statement B: "Photoelectric effect takes place with free electrons."
This is false. The photoelectric effect primarily occurs with bound electrons (especially tightly bound ones), as the entire atom absorbs the recoil momentum, making the process more efficient. Free electrons cannot fully absorb the photon's momentum and energy, so the photoelectric effect is negligible for them.
Conclusion: Both statements A and B are false.
Correct choice: (4) Both A and B are false.

questions.q:
Consider the two following statements $A$ and $B$, and identify the correct choice given in the answers :
(A) In photovoltaic cells the photoelectric current produced is not proportional to the intensity of incident light.
(B) In gas filled photoemissive cells, the velocity of photoelectrons depends on the wavelength of the incident radiation.
questions.solution:
In photovoltaic cells the photoelectric current produced is proportional to the intensity of incident light, so statement $A$ is false.
The velocity of photoelectrons depends on the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons, which depends on the frequency and hence on the wavelength of incident radiation, so statement $B$ is true.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Stopping potential in photoelectric effect does not depend on the power of the light source.

Statement II : For a given metal, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron depends on the wavelength of the incident light.

In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both statement I and statement II are correct
questions.solution:
Stopping potential depends on frequency of incident light and nature of the emitter material. It is independent of the power of the light source.

Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is stated asKEmax=hν-ϕ=hcλ-ϕ, Where, h is the Planck’s constant, ν is the frequency, λ is wavelength of incident light and ϕ is the work function of the metal surface.

Thus, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron depends on the wavelength of the incident light.

So both statements I and II are correct

Statement II: If the wavelength of the photon is decreased, then the momentum and energy of a photon will also decrease.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are false
Both Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> and Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> are true
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is true but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is false
Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">I</mi></math> is false but Statement <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>II</mi></math> is true
questions.solution:
If linear momentum are equal then wavelength also equal.

The momentum p and energy E of a photon is given by,

p=hλ, E=hcλ; where c is speed of light and h is Plank's constant.

On decreasing wavelength, momentum and energy of photon increases.

questions.q:
Statement (I) : By increasing the potential difference between cathode and anode continuously in a photoelectric experiment, the photo current always increases continuously.
Statement (II) : If two photons A and B of energies 2.5 $\mathrm{eV}$ and $3.5 \mathrm{eV}$ respectively fall on a metal surface of work function $2.0 \mathrm{eV}$, then the ratio of maximum kinetic energies emitted between A and B is 3 .
Statement (III) : The maximum energy needed by an electron to come out from metal surface is called the work function of the metal.
Which of the following is correct?
options: Statements I, II and III are true
Statements I, II are true, but statement III is false
Statements II, III are true, but statement I is false
Statements I, II and III are false
questions.solution:
Photocurrent will become constant after a certain potential difference between cathode and anode.
So, (I) is incorrect
Now,
$\frac{(\mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E})_{\mathrm{A}}}{(\mathrm{K} . \mathrm{E})_{\mathrm{B}}}=\frac{2.5-2}{3.5-2}=\frac{0.5}{1.5}=\frac{1}{3}$
So, (II) is incorrect
Work function is minimum energy needed to eject the electron.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Two photons each of energy 3 eV, can't eject electrons from a surface of work function 5 eV.
Reason (R) : Only a photon of energy greater than work function may emit photoelectron. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): Two photons, each with energy of 3 eV, cannot eject electrons from a surface with a work function of 5 eV. This is because the energy required to eject an electron (the work function) is 5 eV, but each photon only carries 3 eV. Photons interact with electrons individually, so the combined energy of two photons is irrelevant in this context. Hence, (A) is true.
- Reason (R): The photoelectric effect occurs when a photon with energy greater than the work function strikes the surface. If the photon's energy is less than the work function, no electrons will be emitted, regardless of the number of photons. Therefore, \((\mathrm{R})\) is true and correctly explains (A).

questions.q:
Two statements are given below :
Statement I : Photosensitivity of a metal is high, if its work function is low.
Statement II : Work function for a metal is given by \(\mathrm{hv}_0\), where \(\mathrm{v}_{\mathrm{o}}\) is threshold frequency. Considering the above, choose the appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct and statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect and statement II is correct.
Both statements I and statements II are incorrect.
questions.solution:
- Statement I: Photosensitivity refers to how easily electrons can be ejected from a metal when exposed to light. If the metal has a lower work function, less energy is required to release electrons, making it more photosensitive. Thus, Statement I is correct.
- Statement II: The work function (\(\phi\)) of a metal is indeed given by \(\ddot{I} 0=h \hat{I} 1 / 20\), where \(h\) is Planck's constant and \(\hat{I}^{1 / 20}\) is the threshold frequency. This is based on the photoelectric effect theory. Thus, Statement II is also correct.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : In Davisson-Germer experiment wavelength associated with the beam decreases with increases of speed of electrons.
Reason (R) : Wavelength associated with electron beam in Davission-Germer experiment is given by \(\lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mK}}}\)
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of \((\mathrm{A})\).
questions.solution:
To analyze the statements:
Assertion (A): "In Davisson-Germer experiment, the wavelength associated with the beam decreases with an increase in the speed of electrons."
- This statement is true. According to de Broglie's hypothesis, the wavelength \(\lambda\) is inversely proportional to the momentum \(p\) of the particle, which is related to its speed. As the speed of electrons increases, the wavelength decreases.
Reason (R): "Wavelength associated with the electron beam in Davisson-Germer experiment is given by \(\lambda=\frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}\)."
- This statement is also true. The formula given represents the de Broglie wavelength for particles, where \(h\) is Planck's constant, \(m\) is the mass of the electron, and \(K\) is the kinetic energy.

questions.q:
In photoelectric effect
A. The photocurrent is proportional to the intensity of the incident radiation.
B. Maximum kinetic energy with which photoelectrons are emitted depends on the intensity of incident light.
C. Max K.E. with which photoelectrons are emitted depends on the frequency of incident light.
D. The emission of photoelectrons require a minimum threshold intensity of incident radiation.
E. Max K.E. of the photoelectrons is independent of the frequency of the incident light.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
With proper energetic radiation, the photoelectric current increases with an increase in accelerating potential until it reaches a point where it reaches its maximum and does not increase with an additional increase in accelerating potential.

For a given potential difference, the photocurrent is directly proportional to the intensity of the incident radiation.

The maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons can be written as

Kmax=hν-φ

From above equation, it can be seen that the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron depends on the frequency of the light used.

Hence, the statements A and C are correct.

questions.q:
From the photoelectric effect experiment, following observations are made. Identify which of these are correct
A. The stopping potential depends only on the work function of the metal.
B. The saturation current increases as the intensity of incident light increases.
C. The maximum kinetic energy of a photo electron depends on the intensity of the incident light.
D. Photoelectric effect can be explained using wave theory of light.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Stopping potential depends on both frequency of light and work function.
(B) Saturation current ∝ intensity of light.
(C) Maximum KE depends on frequency.
(D) Photoelectric effect is explained using particle theory. In this phenomenon, when electromagnetic radiation (such as light) hits the material, the emission of electrons takes place. In the photoelectric effect, if the frequency is too low, no electron is seen getting freed. But, if the frequency is high enough, some electrons can be observed. These observations prove that the Light is made of particles. The energy of the particle increases with the frequency.

The threshold wavelength for photoelectric emission from a material is 5500 A∘. Photoelectrons will be emitted, when this material is illuminated with monochromatic radiation from a

A. 75 W infra-red lamp

B. 10 W infra-red lamp

C. 75 W ultra-violet lamp

D. 10 W ultra-violet lamp

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Given here, threshold wavelength λth=5500 Å=550 nm

For photoelectric emission, the wavelength of the light should be less than 550 nm.

Wavelength of infrared radiation extends from 700 nm-1 mm and that of ultraviolet radiation is 100-400 nm.

Since, UV light has less wavelength than 550 nm, so only UV would be able to emit photoelectrons.

questions.q:
With reference to the observations in photo-electric effect, identify the correct statements from below:

A. The square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.

B. The value of saturation current increases on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.

C. The maximum kinetic energy of photo-electrons decreases on decreasing the power of LED (light emitting diode) source of light.

D. The immediate emission of photo-electrons out of metal surface can not be explained by particle nature of light/electromagnetic waves.
E. Existence of threshold wavelength can not be explained by wave nature of light/electromagnetic waves.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
From Einstein's photoelectric equation, 

Maximum kinetic energy, KEmax=12mvmax2=hf-ϕ, where, vmax is maximum velocity of photoelectrons, h is Planck's constant, f is frequency of incident light and ϕ is work function of metal.

From above relation, we can see that the square of maximum velocity of photoelectrons varies linearly with frequency of incident light.

If we increase the intensity of the incident radiation by keeping the frequency constant, then the value of saturation current increases in proportion to the intensity of the incident radiation. Thus, saturation current decreases on moving the source of light away from the metal surface.

The kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is directly proportional to the light frequency, and it remains constant as light amplitude or power of source increases.

Photoelectric effect cannot be explained on the basis of wave nature because experimentally a particular energy called the work function of the metal surface in needed to eject electrons from surface, irrespective of the time for which light is incident. 

Photoelectric effect can be explained by particle nature of light (i.e. quantum theory). Threshold wavelength is maximum wavelength at which emission takes place.

questions.q:
For photoelectric effect which of the following statements are true.
I) The kinetic energies of the photoelectrons do not depend on the frequency of light
II) Photoelectric effect will always occur for highly intense light
III) The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectron does not depend upon the intensity of the light
IV) The escaping electron's kinetic energy is larger for larger frequency
questions.solution:
The maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectrons depends on the frequency of incident light and does not depend on the intensity of light.

Kmax=hν-ϕ

Therefore, statement III and IV are correct and I is incorrect.

Photoelectric effect happens when insident radiation ha frequency greater than minimum frequency called as threshold frequency. Therefore, statement II is incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the column I with column II -
\(\begin{array}{|c|l|c|l|}
\hline
& \text{Column-I (Radiation)} & & \text{Column-II (Source)} \\
\hline
(A) & \text{X-rays} & (P) & \text{Nuclei of atoms and sudden deceleration of} \\
  &  &  & \text{high-energy free electrons} \\
\hline
(B) & \text{Gamma rays} & (Q) & \text{Inner electrons in atoms and sudden deceleration} \\
  &  &  & \text{of high-energy free electrons} \\
\hline
(C) & \text{Radiowaves} & (R) & \text{Oscillating electric circuit} \\
\hline
(D) & \text{Infrared} & (S) & \text{Outer electrons in atoms and molecules} \\
\hline
(E) & \text{Ultraviolet} & (T) & \text{Outer electrons in atoms} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
- (A) X-rays \(\rightarrow\) (Q) Inner electrons in atoms and sudden deceleration of high energy free electrons: X-rays are produced when high-energy electrons collide with atoms, causing inner electrons to be ejected, or when free electrons are suddenly decelerated.
- (B) Gamma rays \(\rightarrow\) (P) Nuclei of atoms and sudden deceleration of high energy free electrons: Gamma rays are emitted from the nuclei of atoms during radioactive decay or nuclear reactions.
- (C) Radiowaves \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{R})\) Oscillating electric circuit:
Radiowaves are generated by oscillating electric circuits, such as those in radio transmitters.
- (D) Infrared \(\rightarrow\) (S) Outer electrons in atoms and molecules:
Infrared radiation is often emitted due to the transitions of outer electrons in atoms and molecules, typically associated with thermal motion.
- (E) Ultraviolet \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{T})\) Outer electrons in atoms: Ultraviolet radiation is produced when outer electrons in atoms undergo transitions to lower energy levels.
Thus, the correct matching is:
\(A \rightarrow Q, B \rightarrow P, C \rightarrow R, D \rightarrow S, E \rightarrow T .\)

questions.q:
On a photositive surface of threshold wavelength \(5 \lambda\), two different monochromatic beams of wavelengths \(3 \lambda\) and \(\lambda\) are incident, one after another, then match the ratio of physical quantities specified in column - I to the ratio values given in column - II.
\(\begin{array}{|c|l|c|l|}
\hline
& \text{Column I} & & \text{Column II} \\
\hline
(a) & \text{Maximum KE of photo electrons} & (i) & 1 : 3 \\
\hline
(b) & \text{Speed of incident photons} & (ii) & 1 : 6 \\
\hline
(c) & \text{Momentum of incident photons} & (iii) & 1 : \sqrt{6} \\
\hline
(d) & \text{Fastest speeds of photo electrons} & (iv) & 1 : 1 \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.solution: \(\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{K}_1=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{3 \lambda}-\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{5 \lambda}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}\left[\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{5}\right]=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}\left[\frac{2}{15}\right] \\ & \mathrm{K}_2=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}-\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{5 \lambda}=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}\left[1-\frac{1}{5}\right]=\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}\left[\frac{4}{5}\right] \end{aligned}\) (a) Ratio of KE \(\frac{\mathrm{K}_1}{\mathrm{~K}_2}=\frac{\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}\left[\frac{2}{15}\right]}{\frac{\mathrm{hc}}{\lambda}\left[\frac{4}{5}\right]}=\frac{1}{6}=1: 6\) (b) Ratio of speeds of incident photons \(\frac{c_1}{c_2}=\frac{1}{1}=1: 1\) Ratio of momentum of incident photons \(\frac{\mathrm{p}_1}{\mathrm{p}_2}=\frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1}=\frac{\lambda}{3 \lambda}=1: 3\) (c) Ratio of fastest speed of photo electrons \(\frac{v_1}{v_2}=\sqrt{\frac{K_1}{K_2}}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{6}}=1: \sqrt{6}\)

Match the column I with column II -
\(\begin{array}{|c|l|c|l|}
\hline
& \text{Column-I (Radiation)} & & \text{Column-II (Use)} \\
\hline
(A) & \gamma\text{-rays} & (P) & \text{Structure of crystal} \\
\hline
(B) & \text{X-rays} & (Q) & \text{Structure of nuclei} \\
\hline
(C) & \text{Microwaves} & (R) & \text{Radar and radio broadcasting} \\
\hline
(D) & \text{Infrared} & (S) & \text{Long distance wireless communication} \\
  &  &  & \text{via satellite} \\
\hline
(E) & \text{Radio waves} & (T) & \text{Structure of molecules} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
- (A) V -rays \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{P})\) Structure of crystal: Gamma rays are used in diffraction studies to analyze the crystal structure.
- (B) X-rays \(\rightarrow\) (Q) Structure of nuclei: X-rays can be used to investigate the structure of nuclei through various techniques in nuclear physics.
- (C) Microwaves \(\rightarrow\) (S) Long distance wireless communication via satellite: Microwaves are commonly used for satellite communications, including long-distance wireless communication.
- (D) Infrared \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{T})\) Structure of molecules:
Infrared radiation is used in spectroscopy to study the vibrational and rotational transitions in molecules, providing information about their structure.
- \((\mathrm{E})\) Radio waves \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{R})\) Radar and radio broadcasting:
Radio waves are utilized in radar technology and for radio broadcasting.
Thus, the correct matching is:
\(A \rightarrow P, B \rightarrow Q, C \rightarrow S, D \rightarrow T, E \rightarrow R .\)

questions.q:
Match the column I with column II -
\(\begin{array}{|c|l|c|l|}
\hline
& \text{Column-I} & & \text{Column-II} \\
\hline
(A) & \text{Force between a proton and a proton} & (P) & \text{Gravitational force} \\
  & \text{inside nucleus} &  & \\
\hline
(B) & \text{Force between a proton and a neutron} & (Q) & \text{Electrostatic force} \\
  & \text{inside nucleus} &  & \\
\hline
(C) & \text{Force on an electron in an atom} & (R) & \text{Strong force} \\
\hline
(D) & \text{Conservative force} & (S) & \text{Weak force} \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
questions.solution:
- (A) Force between a proton and a proton inside the nucleus \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{R})\) Strong force: The force between two protons in the nucleus is primarily the strong nuclear force, which is responsible for holding the nucleus together despite the electrostatic repulsion between the positively charged protons.
- (B) Force between a proton and a neutron inside the nucleus \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{R})\) Strong force:
The force between a proton and a neutron is also the strong nuclear force, which is the dominant force acting within the nucleus.
- (C) Force on an electron in an atom
\(\rightarrow\) (Q) Electrostatic force:
The force acting on an electron in an atom due to the nucleus (which is positively charged) is an electrostatic force (Coulomb's law).
- (D) Conservative force \(\rightarrow(\mathrm{R})\) and (S):
A conservative force can refer to both the electrostatic force and the gravitational force, but in the context of nuclear interactions, the primary focus is on the strong and weak forces. Since both the strong force and weak force are fundamental forces, this option can be interpreted to include both.
Thus, the correct matching is:
\(A \rightarrow R, B \rightarrow R, C \rightarrow Q, D \rightarrow R S .\)

questions.q:
Match the following ratio of De-Broglie wavelengths of a proton and \(\alpha\) particle, when both
\(\begin{array}{|c|l|c|l|}
\hline
& \text{List-I} & & \text{List-II} \\
\hline
A & \text{Have same speed} & (p) & 2 : 1 \\
\hline
B & \text{Have same potential} \\ 
  & \text{difference} & (q) & 1 : 1 \\
\hline
C & \text{Have same kinetic} \\ 
  & \text{energy} & (r) & 4 : 1 \\
\hline
D & \text{Have same linear} \\ 
  & \text{momentum} & (s) & 2 \sqrt{2} : 1 \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
options: \(\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline & A & B & C & D \\ \hline 1 & p & q & r & s \\ \hline \end{array}\)
\(\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline & A & B & C & D \\ \hline 2 & r & s & p & q \\ \hline \end{array}\)
\(\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline & A & B & C & D \\ \hline 3 & p & r & q & s \\ \hline \end{array}\)
\(\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline & A & B & C & D \\ \hline 4 & r & q & s & p \\ \hline \end{array}\)
questions.solution:
\(\begin{aligned}
& \text { (A) } \lambda=\frac{h}{m v} \text { or } \lambda \propto \frac{1}{m} \\
& \frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{p}}}{\lambda_\alpha}=\frac{\mathrm{m}_\alpha}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}=\frac{4}{1}\left(\therefore \mathrm{~m}_\alpha \approx 4 \mathrm{~m}_{\mathrm{p}}\right) \\
& \text { (B) } \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mqV}}} \text { or } \lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{~m} \cdot \mathrm{q}}} \\
& \frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{p}}}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\left(\frac{\mathrm{m}_\alpha}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}\right)\left(\frac{\mathrm{q}_\alpha}{\mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{p}}}\right)}=\sqrt{\frac{4}{1} \times \frac{2}{1}}=\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{1} \\
& \text { (} \left.\therefore \mathrm{q}_\alpha=2 \mathrm{q}_{\mathrm{p}}\right)
\end{aligned}\)
(C)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\sqrt{2 \mathrm{mE}_{\mathrm{k}}}} \text { or } \lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{~m}}} \\
& \frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{p}}}{\lambda_\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{\mathrm{m}_\alpha}{\mathrm{m}_{\mathrm{p}}}}=\sqrt{\frac{4}{1}}=\frac{2}{1}
\end{aligned}\)
(D)
\(\begin{aligned}
& \lambda=\frac{\mathrm{h}}{\mathrm{p}} \\
& \frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{p}}}{\lambda_\alpha}=\frac{1}{1}
\end{aligned}\)
